drivingQuestion: Why doesn't 'the edge of the roof descends and seals' apply to a two-sided breach?
outcomeNote: Difficulty answered in the following unit

segments.he: וְכֵן בַּיִת שֶׁנִּפְרַץ מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹתָיו. מַאי שְׁנָא מֵרוּחַ אַחַת, דְּאָמְרִינַן: פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם. מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת נָמֵי לֵימָא: פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם!
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And likewise,» with regard to «a house that was breached» on Shabbat «from two of its sides» into a public domain, the residents are permitted to carry in the house on that Shabbat, but not a future Shabbat. The Gemara asks: In «what» way «is» a breach «on one side different?» The difference is due to the fact «that we say: The edge of the roof descends and seals» the house, as if there were a full-fledged partition there. «So too,» when it is breached «on two sides, let us say: The edge of the roof descends and seals.»

moves.about: mishna lemma on a house breached on two sides

moves.summary: The roof edge should seal two sides as it seals one
moves.about: if the roof edge seals a one-sided breach, it should seal a two-sided one too
